\[
I_{\text{out}}(x,y) = \sum_{j=-r}^{r} \sum_{i=-r}^{r} g_i \, g_j \, I(x+i,\, y+j),
\qquad
g_i = \frac{e^{-i^2 / (2\sigma^2)}}{\sum_{k=-r}^{r} e^{-k^2 / (2\sigma^2)}},
\qquad
r = \lfloor 3 \, \sigma + 0.5 \rfloor,
\quad
\sigma = 1
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(I\): Input channel value
- \(I_{\text{out}}\): Output channel value
- \((x, y)\): Pixel position. x grows to the right and y grows downward.
- \(\sigma\): Standard deviation of the Gaussian in pixels
- \(r\): Window radius in pixels
- \(g_i\): Normalized 1D weight at offset i

Each output pixel is a weighted sum over a square window. The weights come from a Gaussian curve and add up to 1. The 2D weight is the product of two 1D weights, so the filter runs as one pass along rows and one pass along columns.
